content.comment_body: I am working with a [product_name] PLC for my project. My program uses a counter that starts from a preset value, for example, 7. With each iteration, the counter decreases, stopping once it reaches zero. When the counter holds an odd value, output Q1 should be set high; when it's even, Q3 should be high. How can I check whether the current counter value is odd or even?
Because the [product_name] only calculates using integer fixed point numbers, this logic works for counter values up to 32,766. If the counter goes above 32,766, the value is interpreted as 32,767.
That's excellent—it works well in simulation. I plan to test it live soon and will share my feedback afterward.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focused on implementing odd/even value detection in a counter using a [product_name] PLC. It's noted that the platform supports integer arithmetic only up to 32,766, which may limit program reliability for higher values. Nevertheless, users were satisfied with simulation outcomes and planned to validate with real hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a clear technique to identify odd and even numbers in the PLC logic, and they expect that performance in simulation will match results during live operation.
